# UQDA Core v0.1.9

UQDA Core v0.1.9 hardens Windows installation, raises the repository's
supply-chain protections, and refreshes dependencies without dropping Go
1.25.13 compatibility.

## Windows: unsigned packages with x64 installation testing

- x64, x86, and ARM64 installers are published with the explicit
  `-unsigned.msi` suffix while external Authenticode enrollment is deferred.
- The x64 package is installed on a clean Windows runner and tested end to end:
  installed files, persistent configuration, machine `PATH`, service startup,
  version output, and `uqdactl getSelf`.
- The same test uninstalls UQDA and verifies removal of the service, binaries,
  and `PATH` entry while preserving the node identity for reinstall.
- No user should need to edit `PATH` manually after opening a new PowerShell
  window.

After installing the MSI in an elevated PowerShell window:

```powershell
uqda -version
uqdactl doctor
uqdactl getSelf
uqdactl getPeers
```

Verify the checksum before installation:

```powershell
Get-FileHash .\uqda-0.1.9-x64-unsigned.msi -Algorithm SHA256
```

Compare the result with the matching entry in `SHA256SUMS`. These packages do
not carry an Authenticode publisher signature. Windows systems managed with
WDAC, AppLocker, or another policy that requires a trusted publisher may block
them; use an administrator-approved allow rule or wait for a future signed
release. Do not disable Smart App Control, Defender, or an organization security
policy globally.

## macOS

The installer preserves an existing node identity and configuration.

```sh
brew update
brew upgrade --cask --greedy-latest uqda/core/uqda
sudo uqdactl getSelf
```

The macOS package remains unsigned because the project does not use a paid
Apple Developer account. The installer verifies it against the published
`SHA256SUMS` before invoking the system installer.

## Linux and BSD

Debian packages are published for amd64, i386, arm64, armhf, armel, mips, and
mipsel. Release tarballs are available for Linux, FreeBSD, and OpenBSD
architectures listed in the release assets.

Existing installations can use the release updater:

```sh
curl -fsSLO https://github.com/Uqda/Core/releases/latest/download/updater.sh
sudo sh updater.sh
sudo uqdactl getSelf
```

## Container image

The multi-architecture image is published to GitHub Container Registry:

```sh
docker pull ghcr.io/uqda/core:0.1.9
docker pull ghcr.io/uqda/core:latest
```

The image is accompanied by GitHub provenance and an SBOM.

## Reliability and compatibility

- Fixed a TUN segment-drop log call that newer Go vet versions correctly
  rejected.
- Refreshed supported Go dependencies while retaining Go 1.25.13 as the minimum
  tested toolchain.
- Kept `quic-go` on the Go-1.25-compatible release line; Dependabot will not
  propose the Go-1.26-only line until the project's minimum Go version is
  deliberately raised.
- CI covers Linux, macOS, Windows, FreeBSD, OpenBSD, fuzz smoke tests, and
  multi-node mesh scenarios.

## GitHub security and project automation

- Added Dependabot grouped updates for Go modules, GitHub Actions, and Docker.
- Added Dependency Review as a required pull-request gate.
- Added weekly OpenSSF Scorecard results to code scanning.
- Added structured Issue Forms, a pull-request template, CODEOWNERS, and
  repository-specific Copilot instructions.
- Enabled the dependency graph, Dependabot security and malware alerts, private
  vulnerability reporting, Secret Protection, and push protection.
- Protected `main` from deletion and force-pushes; changes require an
  up-to-date pull request, resolved conversations, `All tests passed`, and
  `Dependency change policy`.
- Enabled automatic branch updates, auto-merge, and deletion of merged head
  branches.

## Release integrity

Download `SHA256SUMS` with the selected asset and verify the checksum before
installation. The release also publishes a Sigstore checksum manifest, GitHub
artifact attestations, container provenance, and an SBOM.

## Maintainers

Windows signing is deferred. The workflow keeps an optional SignPath Foundation
path for a future release without storing a private key in GitHub. See
`docs/windows-release-signing.md` for the current unsigned behavior and the
future signing path.
